# Benchmarking Protocol

Each algorithm is run multiple times per instance. For each (algorithm, instance) pair, the following metrics are reported:


- **Energy**: the lowest energy per spin found over all runs;

- **Success probability**: the fraction of runs that reach a reference ground state energy for the instance. The reference used by each contributing group is stated in its notes; for the current SK runs, it is the lowest energy found by any of the algorithms. Energies that match an independently known ground state are marked$^\dagger$;
- **Time to solution** (TTS) [@ronnow2014]: the standard time-to-solution metric  $\mathrm{TTS}_p = \bar{t} \cdot \log(1-p) / \log(1-P_s)$, the expected total time, running independent restarts, needed to be $p$-confident of finding the best-found energy at least once, where $\bar{t}$ is the mean per-run time and $P_s$ is the empirical single-run success probability. This site uses $p = 0.99$, the field's standard convention;

TTS allows algorithms with different trade-offs between running time and success probability to be compared on a common scale. It depends on the hardware on which the runs are executed, which is recorded for every run in the Hardware column. In the current results, the zero-temperature descents run on a single CPU core and the annealing methods on a single GPU. The full parameters of every run are listed in the All section.

Every table row also reports the **Uploader**: the repository folder `experiments/<uploader>/` that contains the implementation of the algorithm, its description, and the submitted results. The uploader name links to that folder. The algorithms themselves are listed on the [Algorithms](algorithms.qmd) page, which also explains how to add new ones.

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

There are no proven ground states for the SK instances, so every row
(Greedy, Random, Reluctant, Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing)
measures success against the same reference: the lowest energy per spin
found for that instance by any of our runs. This includes runs not listed
here, such as scans over the number of temperatures with up to 100 runs per
instance and Global Annealing runs. A run succeeds if its energy is within
$1.5 \times 10^{-6}$ per spin of the reference. Rows whose best energy is
above the reference have success probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing**

Both run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of $10^5$
replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT` schedule
from $T = 1.5$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at $T = 1.5$, and a
final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips accepted only if
they lower the energy, until none does). Population Annealing uses
multinomial resampling. Each instance is run 10 times. A run's energy is the
lowest one it reaches, during the anneal or in the quench, and its runtime
includes the thermalization and the quench.

**Number of temperatures**

For each $N$, each algorithm was run at 6 to 13 numbers of temperatures on
all 100 instances. Each row reports, for that instance, the number of
temperatures with the lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters
column). An instance that an algorithm never solves reports the number of
temperatures that gave its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| $N$ | Population Annealing (1 sweep per temperature) | Simulated Annealing (10 sweeps per temperature) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 25 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 300 | 8, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 37 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 400 | 13, 17, 21, 26, 31, 41, 61 | 2–8, 10 |
| 600 | 19, 26, 31, 36, 46, 61, 91 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 800 | 26, 36, 46, 56, 71, 91, 136 | 4–10, 12, 14, 17 |
| 1000 | 31, 41, 51, 61, 76, 101, 151 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 1200 | 41, 51, 66, 81, 101, 131, 196 | 6, 8, 10–14, 16, 19, 24 |
| 1400 | 51, 66, 81, 96, 121, 161, 241 | 7, 9, 11, 13–15, 17, 20, 24, 29 |
| 1600 | 61, 81, 101, 121, 151, 201, 301 | 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26$^\ddagger$ |
| 2000 | 71, 96, 121, 146, 181, 241, 361 | 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 30, 36$^\ddagger$ |

$^*$ For $N \le 100$ (both algorithms) and for Simulated Annealing at
$N = 200$ and $300$, the rows come from earlier runs with the same settings
but a single protocol for all instances: Population Annealing with 10
temperatures and 10 sweeps per temperature, Simulated Annealing with 100
temperatures and 1 sweep per temperature. Every one of these runs reaches
the reference.

$^\ddagger$ For most instances the best number of temperatures is the largest
one run, so the Simulated Annealing TTS at $N = 1600$ and $2000$ is mostly an
upper bound.

The sweeps per temperature were chosen from tests at $N = 600$, $1000$ and
$1400$. At the same total number of sweeps, Population Annealing with 1 sweep
per temperature succeeded more often than with 10 sweeps per temperature and
fewer temperatures. Simulated Annealing succeeded equally often with 1 or 10
sweeps per temperature, and 10 sweeps per temperature is faster per run.

The Parameters column abbreviates the `summary.csv` fields: $\theta_l$ is
`MCS_per_temperature` and Num. temp. is `number_of_temperatures`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

:::

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

There are no proven ground states for the SK instances, so every row
(Greedy, Random, Reluctant, Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing)
measures success against the same reference: the lowest energy per spin
found for that instance by any of our runs. This includes runs not listed
here, such as scans over the number of temperatures with up to 100 runs per
instance and Global Annealing runs. A run succeeds if its energy is within
$1.5 \times 10^{-6}$ per spin of the reference. Rows whose best energy is
above the reference have success probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing**

Both run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of $10^5$
replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT` schedule
from $T = 1.5$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at $T = 1.5$, and a
final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips accepted only if
they lower the energy, until none does). Population Annealing uses
multinomial resampling. Each instance is run 10 times. A run's energy is the
lowest one it reaches, during the anneal or in the quench, and its runtime
includes the thermalization and the quench.

**Number of temperatures**

For each $N$, each algorithm was run at 6 to 13 numbers of temperatures on
all 100 instances. Each row reports, for that instance, the number of
temperatures with the lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters
column). An instance that an algorithm never solves reports the number of
temperatures that gave its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| $N$ | Population Annealing (1 sweep per temperature) | Simulated Annealing (10 sweeps per temperature) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 25 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 300 | 8, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 37 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 400 | 13, 17, 21, 26, 31, 41, 61 | 2–8, 10 |
| 600 | 19, 26, 31, 36, 46, 61, 91 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 800 | 26, 36, 46, 56, 71, 91, 136 | 4–10, 12, 14, 17 |
| 1000 | 31, 41, 51, 61, 76, 101, 151 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 1200 | 41, 51, 66, 81, 101, 131, 196 | 6, 8, 10–14, 16, 19, 24 |
| 1400 | 51, 66, 81, 96, 121, 161, 241 | 7, 9, 11, 13–15, 17, 20, 24, 29 |
| 1600 | 61, 81, 101, 121, 151, 201, 301 | 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26$^\ddagger$ |
| 2000 | 71, 96, 121, 146, 181, 241, 361 | 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 30, 36$^\ddagger$ |

$^*$ For $N \le 100$ (both algorithms) and for Simulated Annealing at
$N = 200$ and $300$, the rows come from earlier runs with the same settings
but a single protocol for all instances: Population Annealing with 10
temperatures and 10 sweeps per temperature, Simulated Annealing with 100
temperatures and 1 sweep per temperature. Every one of these runs reaches
the reference.

$^\ddagger$ For most instances the best number of temperatures is the largest
one run, so the Simulated Annealing TTS at $N = 1600$ and $2000$ is mostly an
upper bound.

The sweeps per temperature were chosen from tests at $N = 600$, $1000$ and
$1400$. At the same total number of sweeps, Population Annealing with 1 sweep
per temperature succeeded more often than with 10 sweeps per temperature and
fewer temperatures. Simulated Annealing succeeded equally often with 1 or 10
sweeps per temperature, and 10 sweeps per temperature is faster per run.

The Parameters column abbreviates the `summary.csv` fields: $\theta_l$ is
`MCS_per_temperature` and Num. temp. is `number_of_temperatures`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

:::

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

There are no proven ground states for the SK instances, so every row
(Greedy, Random, Reluctant, Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing)
measures success against the same reference: the lowest energy per spin
found for that instance by any of our runs. This includes runs not listed
here, such as scans over the number of temperatures with up to 100 runs per
instance and Global Annealing runs. A run succeeds if its energy is within
$1.5 \times 10^{-6}$ per spin of the reference. Rows whose best energy is
above the reference have success probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing**

Both run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of $10^5$
replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT` schedule
from $T = 1.5$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at $T = 1.5$, and a
final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips accepted only if
they lower the energy, until none does). Population Annealing uses
multinomial resampling. Each instance is run 10 times. A run's energy is the
lowest one it reaches, during the anneal or in the quench, and its runtime
includes the thermalization and the quench.

**Number of temperatures**

For each $N$, each algorithm was run at 6 to 13 numbers of temperatures on
all 100 instances. Each row reports, for that instance, the number of
temperatures with the lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters
column). An instance that an algorithm never solves reports the number of
temperatures that gave its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| $N$ | Population Annealing (1 sweep per temperature) | Simulated Annealing (10 sweeps per temperature) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 25 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 300 | 8, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 37 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 400 | 13, 17, 21, 26, 31, 41, 61 | 2–8, 10 |
| 600 | 19, 26, 31, 36, 46, 61, 91 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 800 | 26, 36, 46, 56, 71, 91, 136 | 4–10, 12, 14, 17 |
| 1000 | 31, 41, 51, 61, 76, 101, 151 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 1200 | 41, 51, 66, 81, 101, 131, 196 | 6, 8, 10–14, 16, 19, 24 |
| 1400 | 51, 66, 81, 96, 121, 161, 241 | 7, 9, 11, 13–15, 17, 20, 24, 29 |
| 1600 | 61, 81, 101, 121, 151, 201, 301 | 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26$^\ddagger$ |
| 2000 | 71, 96, 121, 146, 181, 241, 361 | 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 30, 36$^\ddagger$ |

$^*$ For $N \le 100$ (both algorithms) and for Simulated Annealing at
$N = 200$ and $300$, the rows come from earlier runs with the same settings
but a single protocol for all instances: Population Annealing with 10
temperatures and 10 sweeps per temperature, Simulated Annealing with 100
temperatures and 1 sweep per temperature. Every one of these runs reaches
the reference.

$^\ddagger$ For most instances the best number of temperatures is the largest
one run, so the Simulated Annealing TTS at $N = 1600$ and $2000$ is mostly an
upper bound.

The sweeps per temperature were chosen from tests at $N = 600$, $1000$ and
$1400$. At the same total number of sweeps, Population Annealing with 1 sweep
per temperature succeeded more often than with 10 sweeps per temperature and
fewer temperatures. Simulated Annealing succeeded equally often with 1 or 10
sweeps per temperature, and 10 sweeps per temperature is faster per run.

The Parameters column abbreviates the `summary.csv` fields: $\theta_l$ is
`MCS_per_temperature` and Num. temp. is `number_of_temperatures`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

:::

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

:::

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

There are no proven ground states for the SK instances, so every row
(Greedy, Random, Reluctant, Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing)
measures success against the same reference: the lowest energy per spin
found for that instance by any of our runs. This includes runs not listed
here, such as scans over the number of temperatures with up to 100 runs per
instance and Global Annealing runs. A run succeeds if its energy is within
$1.5 \times 10^{-6}$ per spin of the reference. Rows whose best energy is
above the reference have success probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing**

Both run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of $10^5$
replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT` schedule
from $T = 1.5$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at $T = 1.5$, and a
final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips accepted only if
they lower the energy, until none does). Population Annealing uses
multinomial resampling. Each instance is run 10 times. A run's energy is the
lowest one it reaches, during the anneal or in the quench, and its runtime
includes the thermalization and the quench.

**Number of temperatures**

For each $N$, each algorithm was run at 6 to 13 numbers of temperatures on
all 100 instances. Each row reports, for that instance, the number of
temperatures with the lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters
column). An instance that an algorithm never solves reports the number of
temperatures that gave its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| $N$ | Population Annealing (1 sweep per temperature) | Simulated Annealing (10 sweeps per temperature) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 25 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 300 | 8, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 37 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 400 | 13, 17, 21, 26, 31, 41, 61 | 2–8, 10 |
| 600 | 19, 26, 31, 36, 46, 61, 91 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 800 | 26, 36, 46, 56, 71, 91, 136 | 4–10, 12, 14, 17 |
| 1000 | 31, 41, 51, 61, 76, 101, 151 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 1200 | 41, 51, 66, 81, 101, 131, 196 | 6, 8, 10–14, 16, 19, 24 |
| 1400 | 51, 66, 81, 96, 121, 161, 241 | 7, 9, 11, 13–15, 17, 20, 24, 29 |
| 1600 | 61, 81, 101, 121, 151, 201, 301 | 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26$^\ddagger$ |
| 2000 | 71, 96, 121, 146, 181, 241, 361 | 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 30, 36$^\ddagger$ |

$^*$ For $N \le 100$ (both algorithms) and for Simulated Annealing at
$N = 200$ and $300$, the rows come from earlier runs with the same settings
but a single protocol for all instances: Population Annealing with 10
temperatures and 10 sweeps per temperature, Simulated Annealing with 100
temperatures and 1 sweep per temperature. Every one of these runs reaches
the reference.

$^\ddagger$ For most instances the best number of temperatures is the largest
one run, so the Simulated Annealing TTS at $N = 1600$ and $2000$ is mostly an
upper bound.

The sweeps per temperature were chosen from tests at $N = 600$, $1000$ and
$1400$. At the same total number of sweeps, Population Annealing with 1 sweep
per temperature succeeded more often than with 10 sweeps per temperature and
fewer temperatures. Simulated Annealing succeeded equally often with 1 or 10
sweeps per temperature, and 10 sweeps per temperature is faster per run.

The Parameters column abbreviates the `summary.csv` fields: $\theta_l$ is
`MCS_per_temperature` and Num. temp. is `number_of_temperatures`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |

</details>

:::

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

There are no proven ground states for the SK instances, so every row
(Greedy, Random, Reluctant, Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing)
measures success against the same reference: the lowest energy per spin
found for that instance by any of our runs. This includes runs not listed
here, such as scans over the number of temperatures with up to 100 runs per
instance and Global Annealing runs. A run succeeds if its energy is within
$1.5 \times 10^{-6}$ per spin of the reference. Rows whose best energy is
above the reference have success probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing and Simulated Annealing**

Both run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of $10^5$
replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT` schedule
from $T = 1.5$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at $T = 1.5$, and a
final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips accepted only if
they lower the energy, until none does). Population Annealing uses
multinomial resampling. Each instance is run 10 times. A run's energy is the
lowest one it reaches, during the anneal or in the quench, and its runtime
includes the thermalization and the quench.

**Number of temperatures**

For each $N$, each algorithm was run at 6 to 13 numbers of temperatures on
all 100 instances. Each row reports, for that instance, the number of
temperatures with the lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters
column). An instance that an algorithm never solves reports the number of
temperatures that gave its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| $N$ | Population Annealing (1 sweep per temperature) | Simulated Annealing (10 sweeps per temperature) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 17, 25 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 300 | 8, 11, 13, 15, 19, 25, 37 | 100, 1 sweep per temperature$^*$ |
| 400 | 13, 17, 21, 26, 31, 41, 61 | 2–8, 10 |
| 600 | 19, 26, 31, 36, 46, 61, 91 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 800 | 26, 36, 46, 56, 71, 91, 136 | 4–10, 12, 14, 17 |
| 1000 | 31, 41, 51, 61, 76, 101, 151 | 3–12, 14, 16, 20 |
| 1200 | 41, 51, 66, 81, 101, 131, 196 | 6, 8, 10–14, 16, 19, 24 |
| 1400 | 51, 66, 81, 96, 121, 161, 241 | 7, 9, 11, 13–15, 17, 20, 24, 29 |
| 1600 | 61, 81, 101, 121, 151, 201, 301 | 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 26$^\ddagger$ |
| 2000 | 71, 96, 121, 146, 181, 241, 361 | 9, 12, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 26, 30, 36$^\ddagger$ |

$^*$ For $N \le 100$ (both algorithms) and for Simulated Annealing at
$N = 200$ and $300$, the rows come from earlier runs with the same settings
but a single protocol for all instances: Population Annealing with 10
temperatures and 10 sweeps per temperature, Simulated Annealing with 100
temperatures and 1 sweep per temperature. Every one of these runs reaches
the reference.

$^\ddagger$ For most instances the best number of temperatures is the largest
one run, so the Simulated Annealing TTS at $N = 1600$ and $2000$ is mostly an
upper bound.

The sweeps per temperature were chosen from tests at $N = 600$, $1000$ and
$1400$. At the same total number of sweeps, Population Annealing with 1 sweep
per temperature succeeded more often than with 10 sweeps per temperature and
fewer temperatures. Simulated Annealing succeeded equally often with 1 or 10
sweeps per temperature, and 10 sweeps per temperature is faster per run.

The Parameters column abbreviates the `summary.csv` fields: $\theta_l$ is
`MCS_per_temperature` and Num. temp. is `number_of_temperatures`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes (sapienza)</summary>

**Success probability and TTS**

For $N = 1000$ ($L = 10$) the reference energy is the verified ground state.
For $N = 2744$ ($L = 14$) it is the lowest energy found by earlier long Global
Annealing runs, which is not verified. The reference energies have 5
decimals, so a run succeeds if its energy per spin is within
$5.5 \times 10^{-6}$ of the reference. Rows that reach the reference report
the reference energy. No run went below the reference. Rows whose best energy
is above the reference (all Greedy, Random and Reluctant rows) have success
probability 0 and an infinite TTS.

**Population Annealing, Simulated Annealing and Global Annealing**

All three run on one NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, with a population of
$131072$ replicas (independent replicas for Simulated Annealing), a `logT`
schedule from $T = 1.92$ to $T = 0.1$, 50 thermalization sweeps at
$T = 1.92$, and a final $T = 0$ quench of the population (single-spin flips
accepted only if they lower the energy, until none does). Each instance is
run 10 times. A run's energy is the lowest one it reaches, during the anneal
or in the quench, and its runtime includes the thermalization, the quench
and, for Global Annealing, the training of the MADE network.

| | Per temperature |
|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 10 local sweeps, multinomial resampling |
| Simulated Annealing | 10 local sweeps |
| Global Annealing | 5 global (MADE) steps, each followed by 15 local sweeps |

Global Annealing trains the MADE network for 40 epochs at the start and 1
epoch at each new temperature (batch size 256, Adam, learning rate
$10^{-3}$).

**Number of temperatures**

Each algorithm was run at several numbers of temperatures on every instance,
and each row reports, for that instance, the number of temperatures with the
lowest TTS (tuned per instance, as in the Parameters column). An instance
that an algorithm never solves reports the number of temperatures that gave
its lowest energy. Numbers of temperatures run:

| | $L = 10$ | $L = 14$ |
|---|---|---|
| Population Annealing | 20, 25, 35, 50, 80 | 375, 1000 |
| Global Annealing | 8, 10, 12, 14 (13 and 16 on 10 instances) | 30, 40, 50, 72 |
| Simulated Annealing | 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 200 | 200, 375, 1000, 2000 |

At $L = 14$ no Simulated Annealing run reaches the reference.

**Parameters column**

| Displayed as | Raw name in `summary.csv` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_g$ | `global_steps_per_temperature` (Global Annealing only) | Number of global (population-level) Monte Carlo steps performed at each temperature |
| $\theta_l$ | `MCS_per_global_steps` (Global Annealing) / `MCS_per_temperature` (Population and Simulated Annealing) | Number of local (single-spin) Monte Carlo sweeps performed between global steps (Global Annealing) or at each temperature |
| Num. temp. | `number_of_temperatures` | Number of temperatures in the annealing schedule |
| Schedule | `schedule` | Name of the temperature schedule (e.g. `logT` for logarithmic spacing) |
